page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d3s.16xlarge is an x86_64 big data server instance optimized for high-density storage and parallel processing. Built on the KVM hypervisor, the instance provides 64 dedicated vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon 8369B processors running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. System memory totals 256.0 GB, establishing a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for concurrent computational frameworks.

The primary architectural distinction of the ecs.d3s.16xlarge is its bundled local storage subsystem, which features 381393 GB of local hard disk drive (HDD) capacity. This extreme storage footprint is coupled with an 80 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, ensuring rapid ingestion and transfer across distributed nodes without hardware acceleration, as the platform does not include GPUs.

From an efficiency standpoint, the provision of extensive integrated HDD storage eliminates the dependency on detached block volumes for bulk retention, maximizing storage density per compute node. The configuration exhibits a clear tradeoff between rotational magnetic media latency and raw data capacity, prioritizing throughput and volume over random access performance.

This hardware profile is tailored for large-scale big data architectures, including Apache Hadoop clusters, distributed file systems, map-reduce pipelines, and batch data processing where vast physical capacity and continuous sequential throughput take precedence over low-latency random I/O.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d3s.16xlarge is a dedicated big data instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. It integrates 64 dedicated Intel Xeon 8369B vCPUs operating at 2.7 GHz alongside 256.0 GB of memory, maintaining a 4.0 GB per core ratio. A central characteristic of this instance is its massive bundled storage capacity of 381393 GB across local HDDs, engineered for data-intensive processing. Connectivity is anchored by an 80 Gbps baseline network throughput, while graphics accelerators are absent. Because the platform relies on rotational media, it trades the ultra-low latency of solid-state drives for expansive local data volume and dense cost-efficient storage capacity. The configuration is directly aligned with large-scale big data processing, distributed storage clusters, data warehousing, log analytics, and sequential batch ETL pipelines.
